title: Actors, Sendable, and the data race the compiler can catch

videos.script: Lesson fourteen ran work side by side, and every answer was right. That was luck of a kind. {{race}} Here is the planner's weekly total, added to by eight tasks at once. It compiles without a word. And the first run loses more than a hundred thousand minutes. Then Swift 6 mode reads the same file, and refuses it. {{actor}} The repair is an actor. One word changes, and calls queue up and run one at a time. {{await}} But only between awaits. You will see two bookings both pass a check, and a budget go below zero. {{sendable}} Then the rule for what may travel between tasks. A struct crosses freely. A class is refused, when both sides still use it. {{main}} Then the main actor, which owns the screen. And the one thing a plain task inherits. {{modes}} Last, the switch behind all of it: the language mode, and how a package chooses it. By the end, the compiler finds the race before any test does.
